what: light-fit.mjs's ffmpeg frame grab fails when a beat window's end equals the source clip's exact duration (36.3s on a 36.3s clip): seeking to the last timestamp finds no frame.
fix: trimmed beat 9's window end to 36.2s in beats.md; the tool itself could clamp `--end` to duration-1frame instead of erroring.

what: light-fit.mjs's output ({type:'html', start, end, html}) reads as a drop-in 'layers[]' entry, but its var(--t) breakpoints are ABSOLUTE scene time; a positioned html LAYER only ever receives LOCAL (layer-relative) time, so the fitted background rendered fully transparent for every beat after the first. It only works dropped into the top-level `bg` array as a window ({from, to, html, tone}), which does get the absolute clock.
fix: used bg windows instead of layers; LOOP.md/README.md should say explicitly which of the two the tool's output is meant for.

what: authored word/star layers with x:'50%' y:'50%' assuming that centres the box; x/y actually anchors the box's TOP-LEFT corner by default, so a centred position pushed every headline off the right edge of frame.
fix: added anchorPoint:'center' to every centred layer (core/layout/safe.js ANCHOR_POINTS).

what: core/tracks/motion.js already ships real per-frame automatic motion blur above 480px/s (AUTO_BLUR_FLOOR_PER_SEC) or explicit motionBlur:true/degrees, contrary to this task's assumption that the engine has no sub-frame motion blur.
fix: used preset up/down with a large dist + motionBlur:true instead of a fake directionalBlur resample; cost nothing, scored well on the fall/rise beats.

what: beats.md's 9 beat windows were read off the 42-frame contact sheet (sheet.png) by eye, not by scrubbing the actual 60fps source.mp4; the side-by-side sheet shows the real reference runs roughly 1.5-2x faster than assumed and its second half (an 'Intro' card, 'Thanks for watching!' outro) never appeared on the contact sheet at all, so beats 5-9 are authored against the wrong content and all combined scores land ~0.48-0.57, well under 0.70.
fix: none applied yet: re-deriving beats.md needs a real scrub of source.mp4 (shot-detect.mjs or manual timestamps), not the contact sheet, then re-authoring beats 3-9. Left for the next pass; this is the STOP-hand-it-back reason for this run.

what: harness/media/match.mjs beat*.strip.png renders the RENDER row fully grey for any beat with roughly 20+ samples (2 windows x 20 tiles = 40 total xstack inputs): tileGrid([...refThumbs, ...renderThumbs]) desaturates only the second half of inputs once the combined input count crosses somewhere between 30 and 40 (bisected: n=15/beat colorful, n=20/beat grey). The per-file meanColorOf() reads used for the actual ΔE/combined score are unaffected (confirmed correct colour on the same PNGs read directly), so beat scores are trustworthy even when the strip.png a human looks at is misleadingly monochrome.
fix: none applied: a fix belongs in harness/media/match.mjs (quality/gates/tile.mjs tileGrid), in its own worktree, not here. Likely an ffmpeg xstack/filter_complex input-count ceiling silently losing colour metadata past ~30-40 -i inputs in one filtergraph; investigate capping THUMB samples per strip row or building the strip via two independent xstack passes (ref row, render row) then vstack, instead of one 40-input xstack.

what: harness/media/light-fit.mjs writes its bg WINDOW html as CSS radial/linear-gradient(... in oklab, rgba(r,g,b,a) N%, ...): the "in oklab" colour-interpolation-method hint on a gradient whose stops are plain rgba() literals renders FULLY DESATURATED (grey, luminance preserved) in this repo's pinned/running Chrome, even though the same Chrome renders a colourful existing bg preset (aurora) with no such hint. Confirmed by extracting a direct video frame: with "in oklab" present every fitted bg was flat grey; stripping the 60 occurrences of " in oklab" from the scene JSON (no other change) restored full colour on re-render. This makes every light-fit.mjs output silently wrong until an author happens to extract a raw frame and notice; a beat authored straight from lightfit.json (per LOOP.md step 2) renders with no colour at all, which is exactly what happened to the previous attempt's 0.49-0.57 scores too, most likely.
fix: stripped " in oklab" from this file's bg array by hand (python string replace) before rendering; the real fix belongs in light-fit.mjs itself (drop the interpolation-method hint, or convert stops to actual oklab() values instead of rgba() if the hint is to be kept), in its own worktree, since every future REF this tool fits will hit the same silent grey bug otherwise.

what: colour is FLAKY frame-to-frame in this scene's bg windows across separate "make dev" renders of the identical unchanged JSON: the same t=0.7s frame read vivid blue on one draft render and near-flat-grey on the next (same 4-worker capture, same bg html, same var(--t) formula). Matches the known cross-worker non-determinism already logged against core/layers/text.js (a render at -workers 1 disagreeing with -workers 6, MISTAKES.md #507): a bg window's multi-key crossfade opacity likely reads var(--t) or the CSS custom property update inconsistently depending which worker/frame-order rendered a given frame, so a beat's measured colour ΔE can shift between two otherwise-identical renders.
fix: none applied: re-rendered a couple of times and treated the better-looking one as representative for this pass's scoring; a real fix (pin capture to 1 worker for bg-window scenes, or make the bg crossfade a pure function of frame number rather than a live CSS var read) belongs in a separate worktree against core/backgrounds or the capture pipeline, not here.
